t: Isabella won the throne of Castile through a civil war, a secret marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon in 1469 and the War of the Castilian Succession, ended at Alcáçovas in 1479.
With Ferdinand she restored royal finances and justice, conquered Granada in 1492, sponsored Columbus's voyage that year and so began the Spanish Empire.

Her policy of religious unity brought the Inquisition, the expulsion of the Jews in 1492 and the forced conversion of Muslims after 1502, and her cause for sainthood was suspended in 1991 over the expulsion.
dyk: In 1893 Isabella became the first woman featured on United States postage stamps and the first named woman on a United States coin, the Isabella quarter, both marking 400 years since Columbus's first voyage.
ev: Born at Madrigal de las Altas Torres, daughter of John II of Castile and Isabella of Portugal
At Toros de Guisando, her half-brother Henry IV names her his heir presumptive
Marries Ferdinand of Aragon in Valladolid without Henry's knowledge
Proclaimed Queen of Castile and León at Segovia after Henry IV's death
The treaties of Alcáçovas end the War of the Castilian Succession and secure her throne
Enters Granada with Ferdinand, issues the Alhambra Decree expelling the Jews and sponsors Columbus's first voyage
The Catholic Monarchs break the Treaty of Granada and order Muslims to become Christians or leave
Withdraws from government and dies at Medina del Campo

f.born: 22 April 1451 (Maundy Thursday) at Madrigal de las Altas Torres; daughter of King John II of Castile and of his second wife, Isabella of Portugal
f.died: 26 November 1504 at the Royal Palace of Medina del Campo, of uterine cancer leading to dropsy; buried in the Capilla Real in Granada beside Ferdinand
f.role: Princess and heir presumptive of Castile from 1468; Queen of Castile and León from 1474 to 1504; Queen of Aragon from 1479 as the wife of Ferdinand II; with Ferdinand, one of the Catholic Monarchs
f.known: her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon in 1469; winning the War of the Castilian Succession; the Santa Hermandad and her reforms of the crown's finances and council; the conquest of Granada, ending the Reconquista; sponsoring Christopher Columbus; the Alhambra Decree expelling the Jews; the Spanish Inquisition
